text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- America intensifies military presence in Gulf, prepares for imminent confrontation with Iraq. Stealth warplanes arrive in Kuwait and B-52 bombers are ready in the Indian Ocean. 5,000 soldiers will also be stationed in region within days.
- President Hosni Mubarak orders removal of youth centre in a posh Cairo residential area which was built without a permit. The state will build another centre.
- Arab foreign ministers in Cairo for talks on Israel's procrastination in fulfilling its peace pledges, will also discuss coordinating an Arab position on the peace process.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat tells Al-Ahram: We appreciate Mubarak's decision to link the Cairo economic summit with peace moves.
- Man builds house over ancient pharaoah's tomb, hiding it for 10 years.
- Saddam Hussein backs down. Iraq announces it will not attack allied airplanes.
- Football team Ahli beats Saudi Hilal with a "golden goal" reaches final of Arab clubs championship.
- Pentagon says Iraqi decision is encouraging, American troops continue to arrive in the region.
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross to meet Mubarak in Cairo on September 17 for talks on rescuing the peace process.
- Pharaoh's curse helped capture museum antiquities thief.
- Father slays 20-year-old daughter in the street, says she committed adultery.
- American is massing its troops to attack Iraq. Baghdad promises not to hit American planes.
- Minister of Trade Ahmed Goweli to discuss cotton export prices on Sunday.
- Police are looking for a man who tricked culture minister, saying he found a gold-filled tomb in southern Aswan province.
